Ovidiopol Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ovidiopol, Ukraine

Demolished. Created in the 1870s and marked on a 1917 Russian map, this cemetery was likely demolished during the Soviet period after WWII, though possibly used afterward - neighbors recall the rabbi's mother being buried here about 50 years before this survey, and locals believed gravestones remained until recently, when they were apparently removed. Jewish community mentions date to the mid-19th century, with a synagogue by 1856; population reached 72 by 1865 and 394 (8%) by 1897. A pogrom struck in October 1905; a cemetery operated by 1910, and Jews owned 27 market stalls by 1913. Civil War-era pogroms (1918-1920) drove many away, reducing population to 78 by 1926. Six Jews were murdered in Ovidiopol in September 1941.
